headline: Refining margins roar back, powering a blowout quarter
summary_short: Marathon Petroleum's Q2 2026 net income attributable to MPC surged 322.5% y/y to $5.14 billion ($17.73 diluted EPS) as crack spreads widened across every region, lifting refining margin to $36.33/bbl from $17.58/bbl a year earlier.
summary_long: Refining & Marketing segment adjusted EBITDA nearly quadrupled to $6.7 billion as crack spreads widened across all regions, though crude utilization slipped to 94% from 97% on planned Mid-Con downtime that also pushed refining operating costs to $5.72/bbl. Midstream EBITDA rose 8.4% on higher rates, throughput and equity-affiliate growth, partly offset by divesting non-core gathering-and-processing assets. Renewable Diesel swung to a $258 million EBITDA gain on stronger margins and regulatory credits. MPC returned $2.8 billion to shareholders and held $7.8 billion of cash with no revolver borrowings. MPLX raised its 2026 growth-capex outlook by $500 million to $2.9 billion; MPC's own ex-MPLX 2026 capex plan held at $1.5 billion.

drivers.explanation: Crack spreads widened across all regions, lifting R&M margin to $36.33 per barrel from $17.58 a year earlier and driving higher realized product prices.
R&M segment adjusted EBITDA nearly quadrupled to $6.7 billion on wider crack spreads and higher R&M margin per barrel.

R&M EBITDA nearly quadrupled on wider crack spreads; Midstream grew on higher rates and throughput, partly offset by non-core G&P divestitures; Renewable Diesel swung positive on stronger margins and credit values.
Continued share repurchases reduced the diluted share count; $6.1 billion remained under the buyback authorization at quarter-end.
CEO cited strong planning, commercial and operational execution and completion of yield-enhancing El Paso and Robinson refinery investments placed in service during the quarter.
